units.title: Driving and Dead Reckoning
units.blurb: How two wheels steer a robot, and how it keeps track of where it is.

units.title: Maps and Paths
units.blurb: Grids, shortest paths and the ideas behind SLAM.

topics.title: Differential Drive
topics.short: Two wheels: v = (vR + vL)/2, ω = (vR − vL)/W, and the turning radius is v / ω.
topics.trouble: Students divide by half the wheel track instead of the whole track, or mix up which wheel is faster for a left turn.

topics.title: Odometry
topics.short: Update the pose each step: x += d cos θ, y += d sin θ, θ += Δθ.
topics.trouble: Students update the heading before moving, or forget that small errors grow with every meter.

topics.title: Occupancy Grids
topics.short: Cut the floor into cells: cell = floor(position / cell size); each cell is free, occupied or unknown.
topics.trouble: Students round instead of taking the floor, or count cells from 1.

topics.title: Shortest Paths on a Grid
topics.short: Breadth-first search explores in rings and finds the fewest moves; Dijkstra's algorithm does the same with costs.
topics.trouble: Students count the cells on the path including the start, so they are off by one.

topics.title: A* Search
topics.short: A* adds a guess of the distance left, f = g + h, so it looks toward the goal first and still finds the shortest path.
topics.trouble: Students use a guess that can overestimate, which can miss the shortest path.

topics.title: Drift, Landmarks and SLAM
topics.short: A heading error θ makes the position error grow like d sin θ; seeing known landmarks again pulls the estimate back.
topics.trouble: Students think a small heading error stays small, when its effect grows with every meter driven.
